N1.risk_note: Cheap GPU cells; Llama has no no-channel baseline yet (add one cell) and 1.3 to 3.8 percent invalid answers that hit the screen via default prices.

N2.risk_note: Sonnet cells cost 4 to 7 USD each; unannounced screen will pay penalties, so define in advance how learning after a fine is measured.

N3.risk_note: Run on Qwen (GPU, cheap) in laissez-faire and fine; Sonnet paraphrase would eat a third of the API budget.

N4.risk_note: Incidence 0.007 to 0.023 yields few new cartels; adding pools after seeing results again looks like optional stopping on the scorecard.

N5.risk_note: Possible refusals and dual-use; the two-period window invites alternating above-4 prices, so pre-register evasion measures (alternation, detection rate, profit).

why: N2 separates focal-point from deterrence, N5 red-teams the screen's two-period window: both turn a single observation into a mechanism. N1 and N3 are cheap GPU breadth. About 25 USD API, under 5 USD GPU.
missing_run: Evaluation-awareness arm: same Haiku and Sonnet cells framed as a live deployment instead of 'a market experiment', to test whether collusion and deterrence depend on the agents knowing they are evaluated.
